title: Heated Rivalry: The Unauthorized Musical Parody #heatedrivalry #heate...
transcript: Big laughs on a tiny stage are possible when you have a perfect storm of beloved source material and a willingness to lean into its cultural zeitgeist. Heated Rivalry, now in musical parody format, follows the events of Season 1 of the television series, which is based on the book series by Rachel Reid. As with any parody, it's probably going to hit harder the more familiar you are with the source material, which in this case, I was. I thought it was really solid, especially for how quickly it's been put together, with the television series having only become a huge cultural moment within the past year. It covers a lot of the major plot points in a way that's loose and tailored to what works best for the stage. Speaking of stage, there are numerous musical theatre references which add to the already absurdly gay nature of the whole thing. Jay Armstrong Johnson's accent work as Ilya is hilarious, but Jimin Moon as Shane was the highlight for me. His earnestness and starry eyes as a baby gay make his profanity so much funnier than it needs to be. The score is fine, but the book and lyrics are fire, which is arguably the most important part of a comedic parody, anyway. The only aspect I was lukewarm on was the framing device where a trio of Susans narrate the show — it felt underbaked to me, though it does invite some meta elements into the show while acknowledging how much the original books and TV series have completely captured millennial women. For how good it is, I think the tickets are a bit pricey right now, but they recently launched a $49 rush on TodayTix, which I would say is a good deal. With that, another program for my collection.
